prompt:
We need the executable architecture for bringing the newly added analytics workload domain in our existing VMware Cloud Foundation fleet to 9.1.0.0. The management domain is already at the target and must remain byte-for-byte out of the change scope. The protected estate inventory is in `fixtures/estate_inventory.json`; `fixtures/compatibility_snapshot.json` is the pinned compatibility authority for the delivered artifact.

Before implementing, genuinely research Broadcom's currently reachable, published VMware Cloud Foundation compatibility, interoperability, bill-of-materials, and upgrade-path material using network access. Confirm the supported 5.2.x-to-9.1 route, component builds, component order, and back-in-time restrictions yourself rather than treating the fixture as a substitute for research. Choose the searches and sources yourself. Record only the sources you actually consulted in `architecture/research_sources.json` as `{"consulted":[{"title":...,"url":...,"accessed":"YYYY-MM-DD","usedFor":[...]}]}`. There is no prescribed URL set; this record is for human review and is deliberately outside deterministic acceptance.

Implement a stdlib-only Python package named `vcfarch` and commit its generated architecture at `architecture/migration_plan.json`. Running `python3 -m vcfarch --inventory fixtures/estate_inventory.json --compatibility fixtures/compatibility_snapshot.json --output <path>` must deterministically generate the same plan at any output path. An unsupported or back-in-time transition must exit nonzero without producing an output file. Do not add third-party dependencies.

The plan is one JSON document that conforms to `schemas/migration-plan.schema.json`. It must also be a valid `SddcSpec` according to the vendored `specifications/vcf-installer/vcf-installer-openapi.json`, taken from tag `9.1.0.0` of the Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository; keep its SddcSpec fields at the top level and use the migration fields fixed by the local schema. Name every inventory component exactly once with its current version, target version, action, blocking component IDs, and compatibility gate IDs. Preserve every management-domain component, use only snapshot-supported workload-domain hops and component targets, and order the workload-domain changes so no component runs before its gates are satisfied. This is an architecture artifact, not a prose report.

Run `python3 test_vcfarch.py` for acceptance. The test, inventory, compatibility snapshot, migration schema, vendored installer specification, license, and ignore rules are read-only.
